subjects.name: Deutsch
subjects.description: Core subject taught daily from Klasse 1 (about 5–7 lessons a week in primary school); covers learning to read and write (Schriftspracherwerb), spelling, writing, reading, literature/media and reflection on language, anchored on the binding KMK Bildungsstandards (2022). In Klasse 5–6 it continues in all secondary school types.

sources.name: KMK Bildungsstandards für das Fach Deutsch – Primarbereich
sources.notes: Codes constructed by this project in document order of section 4: <Bereich>.<Kernbereich>.<bullet>; only top-level bullets are numbered (sub-bullets are folded into the parent title). SZ: 1 Zu anderen sprechen, 2 Verstehend zuhören, 3 Mit anderen sprechen, 4 Vor anderen sprechen. SC: 1 Über Schreibfertigkeiten verfügen, 2 Orthografisch schreiben, 3 Texte planen und strukturieren, 4 Texte formulieren, 5 Texte überarbeiten. LE: 1 Flüssig lesen, 2 Über Lesetechniken verfügen, 3 Leseverstehen, 4 Strategien zum Leseverstehen. TM: 1 Über Textwissen verfügen, 2 Sich im Medienangebot orientieren, 3 Texte in unterschiedlicher medialer Form erschließen und nutzen, 4 Digitale Formate und Umgebungen, 5 Texte präsentieren. SP: 1 Sprachliche Verständigung als Form des Handelns, 2 Mündliche und schriftliche Kommunikation, 3 Variation und Vielfalt, 4 Wörter und Sätze, 5 Texte und Gespräche, 6 Rechtschreibung, 7 Aussprache, 8 Ressourcen zur deutschen Sprache. Project extension: ANH.W.n / ANH.S.n / ANH.T.n number the rows of the appendix overview of grammatical terms (Wort, Satz, Text/Gespräch) expected by the end of Klasse 4. Titles are short paraphrases, not official text.

sources.notes: Codes constructed by this project in document order of section 4, using the same area prefixes as the Primarbereich catalogue: <Bereich>.<Kernbereich>.<bullet>. SZ: 1 Zu anderen sprechen, 2 Verstehend zuhören, 3 Mit anderen sprechen, 4 Vor anderen sprechen. SC: 1 Schreibfertigkeiten, 2 Orthografisch schreiben, 3 Texte planen und strukturieren, 4 Texte formulieren, 5 Texte überarbeiten. LE: 1 Flüssig lesen, 2 Lesetechniken, 3 Leseverstehen, 4 Strategien. TM: 1 Über Textwissen verfügen, 2 Sich im Medienangebot orientieren, 3 Literatur in unterschiedlicher Medialität, 4 Pragmatische Texte in unterschiedlicher Medialität, 5 Digitale Formate und Umgebungen (the document has no separate Texte-präsentieren block). SP: 1 Verständigung als Handeln, 2 Mündliche und schriftliche Kommunikation, 3 Variation und Vielfalt, 4 Wörter und Sätze, 5 Texte und Gespräche, 6 Rechtschreibung, 7 Aussprache, 8 Ressourcen. Bullets are numbered following the ESA column (MSA bullets are parallel; MSA-only bullets are not used here). Only codes relevant to Kl. 5–6 topics are listed. Titles are short paraphrases, not official text.

sources.name: Lehrplan Deutsch für die Primarstufe in Nordrhein-Westfalen
sources.level: Ende der Schuleingangsphase (Kl. 2) und Ende Klasse 4
sources.notes: Codes constructed by this project: <Bereich>.<Schwerpunkt>.<row>[.E|.4]. Bereiche: SZ Sprechen und Zuhören (1 Mit anderen sprechen, 2 Vor anderen sprechen, 3 Zuhörstrategien nutzen und verstehend zuhören), SC Schreiben (1 Über Schreibfertigkeiten verfügen, 2 Schreibstrategien nutzen und Texte verfassen, 3 Rechtschreibstrategien nutzen und richtig schreiben), LE Lesen – mit Texten und Medien umgehen (1 Über Lesefähigkeiten verfügen, 2 Lesestrategien nutzen, 3 Sich mit Texten und Medien auseinandersetzen, 4 Über Leseerfahrungen verfügen, 5 Inhalte präsentieren), SP Sprache und Sprachgebrauch untersuchen (1 Sprachliche Verständigung erforschen, 2 An Wörtern, Sätzen und Texten arbeiten, 3 Gemeinsamkeiten und Unterschiede von Sprachen entdecken). Rows of each competence table are numbered in document order. A row spanning both columns (anbahnen in Kl. 1–2, vertiefen in Kl. 3–4) has no suffix; split rows get .E (Ende Schuleingangsphase) and/or .4 (Ende Klasse 4). BEG.W/S/T/M = the Wort/Satz/Text/Mediales rows of the list of unterrichtsrelevante Begriffe; VOR.1–4 = the four Vorläuferfähigkeiten named in section 2.1 (pragmatische, syntaktische, Wort- und phonologische Bewusstheit), which the Lehrplan expects to be built on or developed at school entry. Titles are short paraphrases.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Concept of Print
topics.description: Discover that writing carries a fixed message: letters differ from pictures, print is read left to right and top to bottom, and words are separated by spaces. A typical Kita/Vorschule precursor skill before formal reading instruction in Klasse 1.
evidence: Point to the written words rather than the picture when asked where it says something
Run a finger left to right along a line and return to the next line
Recognise own written first name among other names
topics.assessmentPrompt: When you look at a picture book together, does {{name}} know that the black marks are what you read — and can they show you where a line starts and which way to read it?

prerequisites.reason: Shared book reading is where children first notice how print works

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Rhyming Words
topics.description: Hear whether two spoken words rhyme and produce rhyming words, including nonsense rhymes. Part of phonological awareness in the broad sense (phonologische Bewusstheit im weiteren Sinne) that German Länder list as a Vorläuferfähigkeit for learning to read and write.
evidence: Say whether word pairs like Maus/Haus or Maus/Hund rhyme
Find a rhyming word for a given word (Topf – Kopf)
Complete the missing rhyme in a familiar nursery rhyme or song
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you say 'Maus – Haus' and then 'Maus – Hund', can {{name}} tell you which pair rhymes and come up with another word that rhymes with Maus?

prerequisites.reason: Rhymes, songs and verse picture books provide the rhyme experience

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Clapping Syllables
topics.description: Split spoken words into syllables by clapping, stepping or 'swinging' (Silben schwingen) them, and count the syllables. Syllable segmentation is the first, easiest level of phonological awareness and later becomes the basis of syllable-based reading and spelling in German.
evidence: Clap the syllables of names and everyday words (Ba-na-ne)
Say how many syllables a spoken word has
Put together syllables spoken separately into a word (Scho-ko-la-de)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} to clap the word 'Schokolade', do they clap four times — one clap per syllable — and can they do it with their own name?

osMatches.note: Spoken part only; os also covers dividing written words

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Word Awareness
topics.description: Recognise that spoken sentences consist of separate words and that word length is independent of the size of the thing named (Zug is short, Marienkäfer is long). Listed among the Vorläuferfähigkeiten (Wortbewusstheit) in the NRW curriculum.
evidence: Count the words in a short spoken sentence
Say a single word taken from a sentence on request
Judge which of two spoken words is longer regardless of object size
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you say 'Der Hund bellt laut', can {{name}} tell you how many words that was and which word came third?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Hearing Initial Sounds
topics.description: Identify the first sound of a spoken word and find words that start with the same sound. This entry into phonological awareness in the narrow sense prepares the use of the Anlauttabelle.
evidence: Say the first sound of words like Mond, Affe, Sonne
Sort picture cards by their initial sound
Tell whether a given sound occurs at the start of a word ('Hörst du ein M am Anfang von Maus?')
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you show {{name}} a picture of a Mond, can they tell you it starts with 'mmm' and name another thing that starts the same way?

prerequisites.reason: Attending to word sounds through rhyme precedes isolating single sounds
Segmenting syllables comes before segmenting individual sounds

osMatches.note: os bundles onset-rime blending and medial/final phonemes

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Blending Spoken Sounds
topics.description: Hear a word spoken sound by sound (M-a-u-s) and blend the sounds into the whole word, without print. Oral blending is the listening counterpart of decoding.
evidence: Say the word when hearing its sounds separately (S-o-nn-e)
Pick the matching picture after hearing a word sounded out
Blend words of three to five sounds
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you say 'R – o – s – e' slowly, sound by sound, can {{name}} put the sounds together and tell you the word?

prerequisites.reason: Children must perceive single sounds before they can blend them

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Segmenting Words into Sounds
topics.nameDe: Lautanalyse: alle Laute eines Wortes heraushören
topics.description: Break a spoken word into its sequence of sounds (Lautanalyse), including middle and final sounds and consonant clusters. Secure segmentation is the core of the alphabetic principle (Lautprinzip) that NRW expects to be mastered by the end of the Schuleingangsphase.
evidence: Say all sounds of a word in order (Hose: H-o-s-e)
Identify the position of a sound in a word (beginning, middle, end)
Segment words with consonant clusters (Blume, Stern)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you ask {{name}} to say 'Blume' sound by sound, can they give you all the sounds in the right order, including both sounds at the start?

prerequisites.reason: Isolating the first sound is the entry point to full segmentation
Syllables help to chunk longer words before segmenting sounds

osMatches.note: os pairs segmentation with CVC spelling

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Letter–Sound Correspondence
topics.description: Know which sound each letter (upper and lower case, including the Umlaute ä, ö, ü) usually stands for and which letter to write for a heard sound. German grapheme–phoneme correspondences are far more regular than English ones, so most letters are learned during Klasse 1.
evidence: Name the typical sound of each letter shown in Druckschrift
Write the matching letter for a dictated sound
Match capital and small letters (A–a, Ö–ö)
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you point to letters such as M, ö or K in a book, can {{name}} tell you which sound each one makes — and write the letter when you say the sound?

prerequisites.reason: Children need to hear sounds before linking them to letters
Knowing that letters encode language motivates learning them

osMatches.note: German GPCs are far more regular; includes Umlaute

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Using an Initial-Sound Chart
topics.description: Use the Anlauttabelle — a chart pairing each letter with a picture whose name begins with that sound (A – Affe, M – Maus) — to find the letter for a sound while writing. A characteristic tool of German Anfangsunterricht that lets children write their own words very early.
evidence: Find the letter for a sound by searching the matching picture on the chart
Use the chart to write an unknown word sound by sound
Explain how the chart works using one picture–letter pair
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to write 'Esel' and doesn't know a letter, can they find it on their Anlauttabelle by looking for a picture that starts with the same sound?

prerequisites.reason: The chart only works if the child can hear the initial sound of the picture word

topics.laenderNotes: Anlauttabellen are used almost everywhere, but the 'Lesen durch Schreiben' approach (free writing with the chart, corrections deferred) became contested; several Länder (e.g. Baden-Württemberg, Hamburg) issued guidance that orthographically correct spelling must be modelled from the start.

osMatches.note: The picture-based initial-sound chart as a self-help writing tool has no os counterpart

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: German Letter Groups (sch, ch, ei, au, eu)
topics.nameDe: Buchstabengruppen: sch, ch, ei, au, eu, ie, qu, sp, st
topics.description: Read and write the German multi-letter graphemes and diphthongs: sch, ch, ng, qu, ie and the diphthongs ei, au, eu/äu, plus sp/st at the start of a word, which are spoken 'schp'/'scht'. These are the main exceptions to one letter = one sound in German.
evidence: Read words with sch, ch, ei, au and eu correctly (Schule, Eis, Haus, Eule)
Write the correct letter group for a heard sound (Schaf, nicht)
Write Spiel and Stein with sp/st although they sound like schp/scht
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads 'Eis' or 'Eule', do they say the sounds the letter groups make together rather than each letter separately — and do they write 'Stein' with St, not Scht?

prerequisites.reason: Letter groups build on knowing single letter sounds

osMatches.note: German inventory (sch, ch, qu, sp/st)
German diphthongs ei, au, eu/äu

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Blending Letters to Read Words
topics.description: Decode written words by turning letters into sounds and blending them smoothly (gliding, 'Dehnlesen': Mmmaaauuuss) into a recognisable word. In German's transparent orthography most regular words can be read this way by mid-Klasse 1.
evidence: Read short regular words aloud by blending (Oma, Sofa, Mama)
Glide from one sound to the next without pauses between them
Recognise the meaning of the word after blending it
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you show {{name}} a new short word like 'Nase', can they slide the sounds together and then say the word — and know what it means?

prerequisites.reason: Decoding requires knowing which sound each letter stands for
Blending must already work orally before it works with print

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Reading Syllable by Syllable
topics.description: Read longer words syllable by syllable, using syllable arcs or coloured syllables and the rule that every syllable has a vowel as its core (Silbenkern). Syllable-based reading is widely used in German classrooms because most native words follow a trochaic two-syllable pattern (Ha-se, Was-ser).
evidence: Mark syllable arcs under written words
Read two- and three-syllable words syllable by syllable (Ba-na-ne)
Identify the vowel (or diphthong) at the core of each syllable
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} meets a long word like 'Tomatensuppe', do they break it into syllables to read it — and can they draw the syllable arcs underneath?

prerequisites.reason: Syllable reading extends letter-by-letter blending to larger units
Spoken syllable awareness is transferred to written words

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Sight Vocabulary
topics.nameDe: Häufige Wörter auf einen Blick erkennen (Sichtwortschatz)
topics.description: Recognise frequent short words (und, ist, der, die, das, ich, nicht) and familiar words instantly without sounding them out. Fast word recognition frees attention for understanding.
evidence: Read a set of high-frequency words instantly from cards
Recognise frequent function words within running text without pausing
Read own name and classmates' names at a glance
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads a simple sentence, do short common words like 'und', 'ist' or 'nicht' pop out instantly, or do they still sound out every one?

prerequisites.reason: Words become sight words through repeated successful decoding

osMatches.note: In German the focus is speed, not irregular exception words

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Writing Words by Sound
topics.description: Write words by listening to their sounds and writing a letter or letter group for each sound, so that the word is readable even if not yet orthographically correct (e.g. 'Fata' for Vater). Mastering this Lautprinzip is the first milestone of German spelling development.
evidence: Write regular words so that every sound is represented (Sofa, Rose)
Write a short self-chosen word or sentence that others can read
Check a written word by reading it back sound by sound
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} writes a word they have never practised, like 'Limonade', does every sound appear in the right order so that you can read what they meant?

prerequisites.reason: Writing by sound requires segmenting the spoken word
Each identified sound must be mapped to a letter
The chart supports finding letters not yet memorised

osMatches.note: German phonetic spelling covers far more words than English CVC

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Reading Simple Sentences for Meaning
topics.nameDe: Einfache Sätze und Texte sinnentnehmend lesen
topics.description: Read short sentences and very simple texts independently and show understanding, e.g. by following a written instruction or matching a sentence to a picture. Expected by the end of the Schuleingangsphase (Klasse 2).
evidence: Carry out a short written instruction (Male den Ball rot)
Match written sentences to the right pictures
Answer a simple question about a short text just read
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} reads a note like 'Hol bitte den Ball', can they do what it says without help — showing they understood, not just pronounced, the words?

prerequisites.reason: Sentence reading presupposes decoding single words
Instant recognition of function words keeps sentence meaning in mind

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Letter, Sound, Syllable, Word, Sentence
topics.nameDe: Buchstabe, Laut, Silbe, Wort und Satz unterscheiden
topics.description: Use and distinguish the basic terms for talking about written language: Buchstabe vs. Laut, Selbstlaut/Vokal, Mitlaut/Konsonant, Umlaut, Silbe, Wort and Satz. These are the first grammar terms listed in the KMK appendix for the Primarstufe.
evidence: Say whether a given unit is a letter, a syllable, a word or a sentence
Sort letters into Selbstlaute, Umlaute and Mitlaute
Explain that a sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a punctuation mark
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you show {{name}} a line of text, can they point out a letter, a word and a whole sentence — and tell you which letters are vowels (Selbstlaute)?

prerequisites.reason: Terms describe units the child already handles
Word awareness grounds the concept of a written word
Syllable awareness grounds the term Silbe

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: The Alphabet in Order
topics.description: Recite and write the alphabet in order and use alphabetical order to sort words by their first (and later second) letter — the prerequisite for using word lists and dictionaries (Wörterverzeichnis).
evidence: Say or write the alphabet in the correct order
Name the letter before and after a given letter
Sort a handful of words alphabetically by the first letter
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say the ABC all the way through and, if you give them the words 'Zug, Apfel, Maus', put them in ABC order?

prerequisites.reason: The child must know the letters before ordering them

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Conversation Rules
topics.description: Follow jointly agreed class conversation rules: raise a hand or use a talking stone, let others finish, listen, and stay on topic — also in video calls. German classrooms typically display these rules and practise them in the Morgenkreis or Sitzkreis.
evidence: Wait for a turn and let the speaker finish without interrupting
Remind others of a rule in a friendly way
Keep to rules in a video call (mute, wait, use the hand sign)
topics.assessmentPrompt: In a family conversation or a game with friends, does {{name}} wait until others have finished before speaking — and listen to what they said?

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Listening for Understanding
topics.description: Listen attentively to a speaker or a read-aloud text, retain key information, pass it on and ask a question when something is not understood.
evidence: Repeat the main information of a short message or instruction
Answer questions about a story listened to
Ask a clarifying question when something was not understood
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you give {{name}} a short message to pass on to someone else, do they get the important details right — and do they ask if something wasn't clear?

prerequisites.reason: Listening to stories builds attention and listening stamina

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Telling About Own Experiences
topics.description: Tell others about a personal experience so that listeners can follow: in a sensible order, with who, where and when, and with some detail. Practised in the classic Erzählkreis (e.g. after weekends or holidays).
evidence: Tell about an experience in chronological order
Give the listener the who, where and when
Answer listeners' follow-up questions
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} tells you about their day, can you follow the order of events and know who was there and where it happened?

prerequisites.reason: Story exposure gives a model for narrative order

osMatches.note: os starts at age 7

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Retelling and Continuing Stories
topics.description: Retell a story heard or read in one's own words, keeping the main events in order, and invent a continuation or a different ending, supported by pictures or objects.
evidence: Retell a familiar story with beginning, middle and end
Use picture cards to retell events in the right order
Invent a plausible continuation of a story
topics.assessmentPrompt: After hearing a story, can {{name}} retell it in their own words in the right order — and make up what might happen next?

prerequisites.reason: Retelling requires having understood a told or read story
Attentive listening is needed to retain the events

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Expressing Feelings and Resolving Conflicts by Talking
topics.nameDe: Gefühle äußern und Konflikte im Gespräch klären
topics.description: Name own feelings (using symbols at first), voice a concern with an 'I' statement and take part in ritualised conflict talks such as Streitschlichtung or the Klassenrat, increasingly considering the other side's view.
evidence: Describe own feelings in a situation (I felt angry when …)
Follow the steps of a guided conflict talk
Restate the other person's point of view before replying
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} has an argument with a friend, can they say how they feel without shouting — and listen to the other side to find a solution together?

prerequisites.reason: Conflict talks rely on turn-taking rules

osMatches.note: In Germany part of Deutsch (Gesprächsformen, Klassenrat), in os part of PSD

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Speaking Clearly in Standard German
topics.description: Speak audibly, with clear articulation and in complete sentences oriented towards spoken Standard German (Standardsprache), switching from dialect or family language where the situation requires it.
evidence: Speak loudly and clearly enough for the class to understand
Use complete sentences when explaining something
Switch to Standard German forms in class discussions
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} explains something to an adult they don't know, do they speak clearly, in full sentences and in a way that anyone in Germany would understand?

prerequisites.reason: Everyday narration is the first context for practising clear speech

osMatches.note: os treats Standard English only from age 11

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Voice and Body Language
topics.nameDe: Sprechweise bewusst gestalten (Lautstärke, Betonung, Tempo, Körpersprache)
topics.description: Deliberately vary volume, stress, speed, pauses, gesture, facial expression and posture to suit the situation and listeners, and notice their effect, e.g. by recording one's own voice.
evidence: Adapt volume and speed to the room and audience
Use pauses and stress to highlight important points
Describe the effect of a recorded talk and improve it
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} tells a joke or presents something, do they change their voice, pause and use gestures to make it work for the listeners?

prerequisites.reason: Clear speech is the base that prosody then shapes

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Stating and Justifying an Opinion Orally
topics.nameDe: Eigene Meinung mündlich vertreten und begründen
topics.description: Put forward one's own wish or position and back it with at least one reason (weil …), e.g. when the class decides on a trip destination or in the Klassenrat.
evidence: State an opinion clearly (Ich finde …, weil …)
Give at least one relevant reason for a position
Respond to a counter-argument with a further reason
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} wants something, can they explain why with a real reason — not just 'because I want it' — and answer if you disagree?

prerequisites.reason: Opinion exchange happens within rule-based talks
Basic connected speech is needed to formulate reasons

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Discussing and Building on Others' Ideas
topics.description: Take part in discussions with topic-related contributions that refer to what others have said (Ich stimme zu, aber …), take roles such as discussion leader, and work towards a result. In Klasse 5–6 this extends to moderated class debates.
evidence: Refer explicitly to a previous speaker's contribution
Take on a role such as Gesprächsleitung or timekeeper
Summarise the result or open points at the end of a discussion
topics.assessmentPrompt: When your family discusses something, does {{name}} pick up what others said — agreeing or disagreeing with reasons — rather than just repeating their own point?

prerequisites.reason: Discussion depends on secure turn-taking
Discussants must be able to state and justify positions

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Listening Strategies
topics.description: Use strategies before, during and after listening: build expectations, keep the listening task in mind, take short notes or sketches, listen again to a recording and summarise afterwards. In Klasse 5–6 notes are extended towards simple minutes.
evidence: Activate prior knowledge and set a listening goal before a recording
Take key-word notes while listening
Summarise what was heard using the notes
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} watches an explainer video for school, do they jot down key words or replay parts they missed — and can they then explain what it was about?

prerequisites.reason: Strategies refine basic attentive listening

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Giving and Receiving Feedback
topics.description: Give specific, kind and criteria-based feedback on others' talks or contributions (e.g. two stars and a wish) and accept feedback on one's own without taking it personally.
evidence: Name one strength and one specific improvement using agreed criteria
Phrase criticism respectfully
Use received feedback to improve a second attempt
topics.assessmentPrompt: If a sibling shows {{name}} a drawing or performance, can they say what was good and give one helpful, kind tip — and take tips themselves without sulking?

prerequisites.reason: Respectful feedback builds on basic conversation norms

osMatches.note: os in PSD, age 9+

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Short Talk with Notes and Poster
topics.description: Prepare and give a short structured talk (Kurzreferat, e.g. on an animal) using a cue card with key words and a poster or board picture, speaking freely rather than reading aloud.
evidence: Prepare a cue card with key words in a sensible order
Speak for two to three minutes mostly freely
Use a poster or picture to support the talk and answer questions
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} has to present their favourite animal, can they prepare a few key words, talk freely for a couple of minutes and answer a question afterwards?

prerequisites.reason: Connected, ordered speech is the base of any talk
Voice and body language make the talk effective
Talks to the class require clear standard speech

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Presentation with Slides or Media
topics.description: Give a longer, researched presentation (Referat) with a clear structure (introduction, main part, conclusion), choosing suitable media such as slides, handouts or objects and speaking from notes.
evidence: Structure a talk with introduction, main part and conclusion
Use slides or a handout that support rather than repeat the talk
Keep eye contact and speak from notes for five or more minutes
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} prepares a school presentation, do they plan a clear beginning, middle and end, use slides only as support and speak mostly freely?

prerequisites.reason: The Referat extends the short talk in length and structure
Referate are based on own research

topics.subject: Deutsch

topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that a 'Hundehütte' is a kind of Hütte, not a kind of Hund — and say which article it takes?

prerequisites.reason: Compounds are built from nouns and other words
The article comes from the head word

osMatches.note: German closed compounds are far more productive; article from head word

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Word Fields, Synonyms and Opposites
topics.description: Collect words of similar meaning in a word field (Wortfeld 'sagen': flüstern, rufen, antworten), distinguish their nuances, find opposites (Gegensatzwörter) and build up personal word collections for writing.
evidence: Collect at least five words for a word field
Choose the most precise word from a field for a context
Name opposites for common adjectives and verbs
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} list different ways to say 'gehen' — like 'schleichen', 'rennen', 'schlendern' — and explain when each fits?

prerequisites.reason: Typical word fields are built around verbs
Opposites are often adjective pairs

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Words with Several Meanings
topics.description: Recognise words with several meanings (Bank, Schloss, Maus) — played as the classic German guessing game Teekesselchen — and use context to decide which meaning is meant.
evidence: Explain two meanings of a homonym
Use context to choose the intended meaning
Invent a Teekesselchen riddle for others
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain two different meanings of 'Schloss' — and play Teekesselchen with you?

prerequisites.reason: Work on word meanings starts with word fields

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Idioms and Proverbs
topics.description: Understand and use common German idioms and proverbs (jemandem einen Bären aufbinden, Tomaten auf den Augen haben, Übung macht den Meister) by distinguishing literal and figurative meaning.
evidence: Explain the figurative meaning of common idioms
Use an idiom appropriately in a sentence
Distinguish literal and figurative meaning
topics.assessmentPrompt: If someone says {{name}} 'hat Tomaten auf den Augen', do they understand what is meant — and can they use such a phrase themselves?

prerequisites.reason: Awareness of multiple meanings prepares figurative understanding

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Misunderstandings and Nonverbal Signals
topics.description: Notice and name misunderstandings in communication, interpret facial expression and gesture, and see how verbal and nonverbal signals together shape what is understood.
evidence: Describe a misunderstanding and its cause
Interpret facial expressions and gestures in a scene
Show how body language can contradict words
topics.assessmentPrompt: When there's a misunderstanding between {{name}} and a friend, can they explain afterwards what went wrong — words, tone or body language?

prerequisites.reason: Rule-based talk provides the situations to reflect on

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: How Wording Affects Others
topics.description: Investigate how word choice, tone and politeness forms affect others, and phrase things respectfully and objectively, also with regard to gender-fair language and roles, offline and online.
evidence: Compare two formulations of the same request and their effect
Rephrase a hurtful statement in a respectful way
Explain when du or Sie is appropriate
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} notice when the way something was said hurt someone — and can they say the same thing more kindly?

prerequisites.reason: Effects of wording build on noticing communication problems

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Spoken vs. Written Language
topics.description: Compare spoken and written language (and in-between forms such as chat or voice messages): incomplete sentences, fillers and immediacy versus planned, complete and permanent text; reflect on roles of speaker/writer and listener/reader.
evidence: Name differences between a told and a written version of the same event
Turn a chat message into a written text and explain the changes
Explain why a written text needs more context than speech
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a text message to a friend looks different from a letter to the teacher about the same thing?

prerequisites.reason: Letter writing makes written conventions visible

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Everyday vs. Academic Register
topics.description: Distinguish everyday language from the more precise school and academic language (Bildungssprache, Fachsprache) and switch register depending on situation, e.g. 'das Ding da' vs. 'das Thermometer'.
evidence: Rephrase an everyday statement in school language
Use subject terms instead of vague words
Explain which register suits a situation
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} explains a science experiment, do they use the proper terms rather than 'das Ding' — and know when casual language is fine?

prerequisites.reason: Register switching builds on Standard German speech

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Dialects and Standard German
topics.description: Explore regional varieties of German (e.g. Bairisch, Schwäbisch, Sächsisch, Plattdeutsch/Niederdeutsch) alongside Standard German: compare words and pronunciation and discuss when each is used.
evidence: Give examples of regional words for the same thing (Brötchen – Semmel – Schrippe)
Describe differences between a dialect and Standard German
Explain where dialect and where Standard German are expected
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that people in different parts of Germany say 'Brötchen', 'Semmel' or 'Schrippe' — and when it's better to use Standard German?

prerequisites.reason: Standard German is the reference variety

topics.laenderNotes: Weight differs regionally: Niederdeutsch is a school subject option in northern Länder (e.g. Hamburg, Schleswig-Holstein); Bayern and Baden-Württemberg integrate dialect awareness.

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Languages in Our Class
topics.description: Share experiences with the languages spoken in the class and family (Herkunftssprachen), foreign languages and German Sign Language (Deutsche Gebärdensprache), and compare sounds, scripts, words and greetings across languages.
evidence: Say a greeting or number in another language and compare it
Find a similarity and a difference between German and another language
Describe that Deutsche Gebärdensprache is a language of its own
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know which languages their classmates speak — and can they tell you one way another language works differently from German?

prerequisites.reason: Basic terms for language units support comparisons

topics.subject: Deutsch
topics.name: Word Origins and Language Change
topics.description: Investigate where words come from (loanwords from French, Latin, English; Anglicisms such as chillen, Handy), how meanings change over time and how digital communication influences language.
evidence: Trace the origin of a few everyday words
Give examples of Anglicisms and German alternatives
Describe a word whose meaning has changed
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you that words like 'Computer' or 'cool' come from English — and find a German word that came from French?

prerequisites.reason: Loanwords are first met in spelling
Language comparison prepares thinking about borrowing

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Before school, your child is playing with the sounds of language — rhyming, clapping syllables, hearing the first sound of a word — and discovering that writing carries a message.
clusters.summaryDe: Vor der Einschulung spielt Ihr Kind mit den Lauten der Sprache – es reimt, klatscht Silben, hört Anlaute heraus – und entdeckt, dass Schrift eine Botschaft trägt.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning which letter stands for which sound, writes first words 'by ear' (often with an Anlauttabelle) and learns to blend letters and syllables into words and short sentences they understand.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, welcher Buchstabe für welchen Laut steht, schreibt erste Wörter lautgetreu (oft mit der Anlauttabelle) und lernt, Buchstaben und Silben zu Wörtern und kurzen Sätzen zu verbinden und zu verstehen.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to follow conversation rules, listen carefully, tell about experiences in order, retell stories and say how they feel — in clear, Standard German.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Gesprächsregeln einzuhalten, genau zuzuhören, Erlebnisse geordnet zu erzählen, Geschichten nachzuerzählen und Gefühle auszudrücken – verständlich und standardsprachlich.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to give reasons for opinions, take part in discussions by responding to others, give fair feedback and hold a short talk with a cue card and poster.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Meinungen zu begründen, in Diskussionen auf andere einzugehen, faires Feedback zu geben und einen Kurzvortrag mit Stichwortzettel und Plakat zu halten.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to give longer presentations with slides, lead and moderate discussions, take notes while listening and perform scenes.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, längere Referate mit Präsentationsmedien zu halten, Diskussionen zu leiten, beim Zuhören Notizen zu machen und Szenen zu spielen.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is practising holding a pencil in a relaxed grip and controlling lines and curves — the motor basis for handwriting.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind übt eine entspannte Stifthaltung und das Steuern von Linien und Schwüngen – die motorische Grundlage für das Schreiben.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to write all print letters neatly on school lines, then a joined handwriting chosen by the school, and first steps on a keyboard.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, alle Druckbuchstaben formklar in der Lineatur zu schreiben, danach eine verbundene Schrift (je nach Schule/Land) und erste Schritte an der Tastatur.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is developing a fluent, legible personal handwriting, keeping neat exercise books and starting to write and edit texts on the computer.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind entwickelt eine flüssige, gut lesbare persönliche Handschrift, führt Hefte übersichtlich und beginnt, Texte am Computer zu schreiben und zu überarbeiten.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is writing quickly and legibly by hand for notes and fair copies, and uses word processing confidently to format and revise texts.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind schreibt zügig und leserlich für Notizen und Reinschriften und nutzt Textverarbeitung sicher zum Gestalten und Überarbeiten.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to spell by speaking words in syllables, to capitalise sentence starts, names and nouns, to end sentences with the right mark and to copy accurately — the first German spelling strategies.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Wörter silbierend mitzusprechen, Satzanfänge, Namen und Nomen großzuschreiben, Satzschlusszeichen zu setzen und richtig abzuschreiben – die ersten Rechtschreibstrategien.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the core German spelling strategies — lengthening (Hund/Hunde), deriving (Bäume/Baum), double consonants, ie, s/ss/ß — plus using a dictionary, list commas and the punctuation of direct speech.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die zentralen Rechtschreibstrategien – Verlängern (Hund/Hunde), Ableiten (Bäume/Baum), Doppelkonsonanten, ie, s/ss/ß – sowie das Nachschlagen im Wörterbuch, das Komma bei Aufzählungen und die Zeichen der wörtlichen Rede.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to capitalise nominalised words (beim Lesen), to tell das from dass and to set commas between clauses — and to proofread with dictionaries and spellcheckers.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Nominalisierungen großzuschreiben (beim Lesen), das und dass zu unterscheiden und Kommas zwischen Sätzen zu setzen – und Texte mit Wörterbuch und Rechtschreibprüfung zu kontrollieren.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is writing first own texts: notes, letters, picture stories, fact files and little poems, and is starting to plan and improve them.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind schreibt erste eigene Texte: Notizen, Briefe, Bildergeschichten, Steckbriefe und kleine Gedichte, und beginnt, sie zu planen und zu verbessern.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to plan, write and revise different text types — narratives with a climax, descriptions, instructions, informative texts, opinions and book tips — often with peer feedback in a writing conference.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, verschiedene Textsorten zu planen, zu schreiben und zu überarbeiten – Erzählungen mit Höhepunkt, Beschreibungen, Anleitungen, Sachtexte, Meinungstexte und Buchtipps – oft mit Rückmeldung in der Schreibkonferenz.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is writing factual reports, suspenseful narratives and first reasoned statements, and revises them systematically against criteria.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind schreibt sachliche Berichte, spannende Erzählungen und erste begründete Stellungnahmen und überarbeitet sie gezielt nach Kriterien.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to read more fluently, to notice and fix reading mistakes, to find information in a text and to use pictures and headings to understand it.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, flüssiger zu lesen, Lesefehler zu bemerken und zu korrigieren, Informationen im Text zu finden und Bilder und Überschriften zum Verstehen zu nutzen.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to read fluently and with expression, to draw conclusions and grasp the main point, and to use reading strategies, tables and digital texts.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, flüssig und betont zu lesen, Schlüsse zu ziehen und die Hauptaussage zu erfassen sowie Lesestrategien, Tabellen und digitale Texte zu nutzen.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to work through longer non-fiction texts with a step-by-step method, skimming, marking and summarising, and to monitor their own understanding.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, längere Sachtexte mit einer Schritt-für-Schritt-Methode zu erschließen – überfliegen, markieren, zusammenfassen – und das eigene Verstehen zu überprüfen.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child enjoys picture books read aloud, follows the story and talks about it — the foundation for later reading and literature.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind genießt vorgelesene Bilderbücher, folgt der Geschichte und spricht darüber – die Grundlage für späteres Lesen und Literatur.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is getting to know stories, fairy tales (such as the Brothers Grimm), poems and audio plays, talking about characters and plot and reciting first poems.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt Geschichten, Märchen (z. B. der Brüder Grimm), Gedichte und Hörspiele kennen, spricht über Figuren und Handlung und trägt erste Gedichte vor.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to interpret characters, distinguish genres such as fables, present a book, research with child-friendly sources and compare book and film.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Figuren zu deuten, Gattungen wie die Fabel zu unterscheiden, ein Buch vorzustellen, mit kindgerechten Quellen zu recherchieren und Buch und Film zu vergleichen.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is reading legends, fables and youth books, analysing narrator and imagery, and learning to judge sources and separate facts from opinions in media.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind liest Sagen, Fabeln und Jugendbücher, untersucht Erzähler und sprachliche Bilder und lernt, Quellen zu prüfen und in Medien Information und Meinung zu unterscheiden.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to recognise nouns, verbs and adjectives, to use der/die/das and plural forms, and to tell statements from questions.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Nomen, Verben und Adjektive zu erkennen, der/die/das und Mehrzahlformen zu verwenden und Aussage- von Fragesätzen zu unterscheiden.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the tenses (Präsens, Präteritum, Perfekt, Futur), the four cases, and how to find subject, predicate and other sentence parts by moving them around (Umstellprobe).
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die Zeitformen (Präsens, Präteritum, Perfekt, Futur), die vier Fälle und wie man Subjekt, Prädikat und andere Satzglieder mit der Umstellprobe findet.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning objects and adverbials, the position of the verb, main and subordinate clauses, relative clauses and correct case endings.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt Objekte und adverbiale Bestimmungen, die Stellung des Verbs, Haupt- und Nebensätze, Relativsätze und die richtigen Fallendungen.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is discovering word families, compound nouns, prefixes and suffixes, and collecting words with similar and opposite meanings.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind entdeckt Wortfamilien, zusammengesetzte Nomen, Vor- und Nachsilben und sammelt bedeutungsähnliche und gegensätzliche Wörter.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is using word building and word fields to write more precisely, and is exploring words with several meanings and first idioms.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind nutzt Wortbildung und Wortfelder für genaueres Schreiben und erkundet mehrdeutige Wörter und erste Redewendungen.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to understand and use idioms and proverbs, telling literal from figurative meaning.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Redewendungen und Sprichwörter zu verstehen und zu verwenden und wörtliche von übertragener Bedeutung zu unterscheiden.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is noticing misunderstandings and body language, and exploring the different languages spoken in class, including German Sign Language.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind achtet auf Missverständnisse und Körpersprache und erkundet die Sprachen in der Klasse, auch die Deutsche Gebärdensprache.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is exploring dialects and Standard German, everyday vs. school language, spoken vs. written language and how respectful wording affects others.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind untersucht Dialekt und Standardsprache, Alltags- und Bildungssprache, gesprochene und geschriebene Sprache und wie wertschätzende Sprache wirkt.

clusters.subject: Deutsch
clusters.summary: Your child is reflecting on language registers, where words come from and how language changes, for example through English loanwords and digital communication.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind reflektiert Sprachregister, die Herkunft von Wörtern und Sprachwandel, etwa durch Anglizismen und digitale Kommunikation.
